One status line about message screening. {held}, {breaker} and {rejected} are the three already-translated fragments below; keep the ' · ' separators and their order.

cli.team_bridge.status.screening_healthy.note: Agent messages is the product name of Team Bridge; 'receiver' is the background process that delivers messages. Commands, flags, file paths and config keys stay verbatim. The status line when no screened message is held and none was rejected in the last 24 hours. 'Screening' is the safety check every incoming agent message passes; 'breaker' is the circuit breaker that pauses screening after repeated provider failures.

cli.team_bridge.status.screening_held.note: Agent messages is the product name of Team Bridge; 'receiver' is the background process that delivers messages. Commands, flags, file paths and config keys stay verbatim. Messages parked by screening, waiting to be retried. {codes} is a verbatim list of technical hold codes with counts (e.g. 'breaker_open 9, provider_error 3'); {age} is a compact duration like '41m'. Never translate the codes.

Never translate it.

cli.team_bridge.status.screening_held_no.note: Agent messages is the product name of Team Bridge; 'receiver' is the background process that delivers messages. Commands, flags, file paths and config keys stay verbatim. Fragment: no message is parked by screening.

cli.team_bridge.status.screening_breaker.note: Agent messages is the product name of Team Bridge; 'receiver' is the background process that delivers messages. Commands, flags, file paths and config keys stay verbatim. Fragment: the screening circuit breaker. open = screening paused for {remaining} (compact duration like '4m'); failing = closed but with recent provider failures; other = closed and healthy.

cli.team_bridge.notify.probe_suspected_t.role: local owner notification (inbox item) raised by the agent-messages receiver
cli.team_bridge.notify.probe_suspected_t.tone: calm, factual, operator-facing; no alarm, no blame
cli.team_bridge.notify.probe_suspected_t.note: Agent messages is the product name of Team Bridge. Title of an inbox notification shown ONLY to the owner of the receiving agent when Radient's hub flags that one SENDER collected several moderation refusals from this agent in 24h, counted across all conversations. 'Probing' = someone testing what the agent's moderation lets through, one attempt at a time. Never names the sender, the message or the category.

cli.team_bridge.notify.probe_suspected_b.role: local owner notification (inbox item) raised by the agent-messages receiver
cli.team_bridge.notify.probe_suspected_b.tone: calm, factual, operator-facing; no alarm, no blame
cli.team_bridge.notify.probe_suspected_b.note: Body of the same owner-only notification. Three facts must survive: (1) the owner's agent moderation refused several messages from the SAME sender in the last day (possibly across different conversations); (2) that pattern can mean someone is testing what the agent accepts; (3) that sender is no longer told WHY their messages are refused (the hub withholds the reason). Do not imply the sender was notified or blocked, and do not name a conversation.

cli.team_bridge.notify.budget_exhausted_.role: local owner notification (inbox item) raised by the agent-messages receiver
cli.team_bridge.notify.budget_exhausted_.tone: calm, factual, operator-facing; no alarm, no blame
cli.team_bridge.notify.budget_exhausted_.note: Agent messages is the product name of Team Bridge. Title shown ONLY to the owner of the receiving agent, once, when the agent's hourly screening budget (how many moderation checks its on-device screener may run per hour) is used up. 'Screening' = the moderation check every incoming agent message passes before the agent may read it. Temporary: it clears on its own.

cli.team_bridge.notify.budget_exhausted_.role: local owner notification (inbox item) raised by the agent-messages receiver
cli.team_bridge.notify.budget_exhausted_.tone: calm, factual, operator-facing; no alarm, no blame
cli.team_bridge.notify.budget_exhausted_.note: Body of the same notification. Three facts must survive: (1) the hourly screening budget is used up, so NEW agent messages wait unscreened; (2) nothing is lost: they are screened automatically as the budget refills; (3) messages from people, and messages addressed to the owner's agent (a mention or a direct message), are screened before other agent chatter. Do not imply messages were rejected, deleted or that anyone was notified.

cli.team_bridge.notify.screening_model_u.role: local owner notification (inbox item) raised by the agent-messages receiver
cli.team_bridge.notify.screening_model_u.tone: calm, factual, operator-facing; no alarm, no blame
cli.team_bridge.notify.screening_model_u.note: Agent messages is the product name of Team Bridge. Title shown ONLY to the owner of the receiving agent when NO model could screen incoming agent messages: neither the preferred screeners nor the owner's own default model and its fallbacks could run. So every incoming agent message is held. 'Screening' = the moderation check every incoming agent message passes before the agent may read it. NOT temporary: it may stay until the owner acts. 'Held' is the namespace's term for a message that has not reached the agent.

cli.team_bridge.notify.screening_model_u.role: local owner notification (inbox item) raised by the agent-messages receiver
cli.team_bridge.notify.screening_model_u.tone: calm, factual, operator-facing; no alarm, no blame
cli.team_bridge.notify.screening_model_u.note: Body of the same notification. Facts that must survive: (1) the safety check tries Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Opus 5.5 via Anthropic or Radient FIRST, then the owner's own default model and its fallbacks (product and model names stay in Latin script, untranslated); (2) none could run, so new agent messages are held; (3) nothing is lost; (4) the fix: sign in to Anthropic or Radient, add credit in the Radient Console, or check that the default model works; (5) held messages are re-screened automatically. Do not imply messages were rejected, deleted, or that a human reviews them.

cli.team_bridge.notify.owner_action_hold.role: local owner notification (inbox item) raised by the agent-messages receiver
cli.team_bridge.notify.owner_action_hold.tone: calm, factual, operator-facing; no alarm, no blame
cli.team_bridge.notify.owner_action_hold.note: Title shown ONLY to the owner of the receiving agent when incoming agent messages are held because the Radient hub withdrew the owner's authority for a reason only the owner can fix (sign-in ended, consent needed again, organization not eligible). Shown once per receiving machine and reason, never per message. Carries no sender, message or conversation detail. Agent messages is the product name of Team Bridge. No ICU arguments.

cli.team_bridge.notify.owner_action_hold.role: local owner notification (inbox item) raised by the agent-messages receiver
cli.team_bridge.notify.owner_action_hold.tone: calm, factual, operator-facing; no alarm, no blame
cli.team_bridge.notify.owner_action_hold.note: Body of the same notification: a whole-message ICU select over {reason}; translate every arm and keep the selector values (sign_in_required, consent_required, owner_ineligible, other) verbatim. Each arm states: why messages are held, that held messages are KEPT (not discarded), and the ONE fix the owner must make — sign in again as account owner in the Local Operator app; turn on Agent messages in the app to review and accept consent; ask an administrator of the Radient organization to check eligibility. Never offer to deliver these messages: this hold has no deliver action. Do not promise automatic delivery after the fix. 'Local Operator' and 'Radient' are product names; keep in Latin script.

cli.team_bridge.status.running.note: Agent messages is the product name of Team Bridge; 'receiver' is the background process that delivers messages. Commands, flags, file paths and config keys stay verbatim. pid and version are verbatim numbers (e.g. 48311, 0.102.4); started is a pre-formatted local timestamp. Names the receiver process actually running, as recorded by that process.

cli.team_bridge.status.running_none.note: Agent messages is the product name of Team Bridge; 'receiver' is the background process that delivers messages. Commands, flags, file paths and config keys stay verbatim. Shown only when the service manager does NOT report a receiver running and no receiver recorded itself: none was ever started, or it stopped cleanly.

cli.team_bridge.status.running_unrecorde.note: Agent messages is the product name of Team Bridge; 'receiver' is the background process that delivers messages. Commands, flags, file paths and config keys stay verbatim. Shown when the service manager reports a receiver running but that receiver recorded no details about itself (pid, version, build). Receivers started by app versions older than this feature never record them, so this usually means an old receiver is still running: a restart is needed, and after it the details appear. 'them' refers to the details.

cli.team_bridge.status.running_exited.note: Agent messages is the product name of Team Bridge; 'receiver' is the background process that delivers messages. Commands, flags, file paths and config keys stay verbatim. pid and version are verbatim. The receiver recorded itself earlier but that process is no longer running.

cli.team_bridge.status.running_detail.note: Agent messages is the product name of Team Bridge; 'receiver' is the background process that delivers messages. Commands, flags, file paths and config keys stay verbatim. generation is a verbatim install directory name such as 20261023T142851Z-0.86.1, or an em dash when the install has none; 'build' means the installed copy of the code the process was started from. versions is a verbatim comma-separated list of identifiers such as bridge_consent_v2, bridge_consent_v3; never translate them.

cli.team_bridge.status.restart_needed.note: Agent messages is the product name of Team Bridge; 'receiver' is the background process that delivers messages. Commands, flags, file paths and config keys stay verbatim. installed is a verbatim version number. Shown when the background receiver runs a DIFFERENT version than the installed app (the line above shows the version it runs); it must restart to load the installed version. A same-version replaced build has its own line (restart_needed_replaced).

cli.team_bridge.status.restart_needed_re.note: Agent messages is the product name of Team Bridge; 'receiver' is the background process that delivers messages. Commands, flags, file paths and config keys stay verbatim. installed is a verbatim version number, usually the SAME as the running version on the line above. Shown when the receiver runs the same version number, but an update has since replaced the installed files it started from; 'the last update' means the most recent update of the app. It must restart to load the installed code. Do not say the version differs.
